record.context_brief: Dense Lindelof subspaces off the diagonal
record.original_question: For a topological space X, let Delta be the diagonal {(x,x): x in X}. If X is a GO-space and X squared minus Delta has a dense Lindelof subspace, must X be separable? If X is a Souslin space, can X squared minus Delta have a dense Lindelof subspace?

evidence.quote: Studying properties of a space X off of the diagonal means studying properties of the space X2 \ ∆. For example one can show that a GO-space X is separable if and only c(X2 \ ∆) = ω.
Question 11 ([6]). Is it true that a GO-space is separable if X2 \ ∆ has a dense Lindelöf subspace? If X is a Souslin space, can X2 \ ∆ have a dense Lindelöf subspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space and let Δ = {(x,x) : x ∈ X} denote the diagonal of X × X. Recall:
(a) A GO-space (generalized ordered space) is a triple (X, τ, ≤) where ≤ is a linear order on X and τ is a Hausdorff topology on X having a base of order-convex sets (equivalently, X embeds as a subspace into a linearly ordered topological space).
(b) A Souslin space is a linearly ordered topological space which is ccc (every family of pairwise disjoint nonempty open sets is countable) but not separable.
(c) A subspace D ⊆ Y is dense Lindelöf if D is dense in Y and every open cover of D (by open subsets of Y, equivalently by relatively open subsets of D) has a countable subcover.

Answer the following two questions:

(1) If X is a GO-space and X² \ Δ contains a dense Lindelöf subspace, must X be separable?

(2) If X is a Souslin space, can X² \ Δ contain a dense Lindelöf subspace?
